cards.title: Three kinds of radiator
cards.body: An intentional radiator means to emit. An unintentional radiator makes RF for use inside, or sends it down a wire, without meaning to radiate. An incidental radiator, such as a DC motor or a switch, makes RF only as a side effect. Part 15 is how the first two operate without an individual licence if they follow the rules.

cards.title: Digital device and RF
cards.body: A digital device generates and uses timing above 9,000 pulses per second and uses digital techniques. Radio-frequency energy in Part 15 runs from 9 kHz to 3,000,000 MHz. A personal computer marketed for the home is a Class B digital device.

cards.title: Class A and Class B
cards.body: Class A is marketed for commercial, industrial, or business use, not for the home or the general public. Class B is marketed for a residence, even if it also ends up in an office. You are encouraged to qualify a commercial product to Class B. The Commission can force Class B if a type keeps causing interference.

cards.title: Radiated limits
cards.body: Class B at 3 m is 100, 150, 200, and 500 µV/m. Class A at 10 m is 90, 150, 210, and 300 µV/m. The tighter limit applies at the band edge. Below or at 1 GHz those limits are quasi-peak. Above 1 GHz they are average limits, with a peak cap 20 dB higher.

cards.title: Conducted limits
cards.body: Class B slopes from 66 to 56 dBµV quasi-peak (56 to 46 average) between 0.15 and 0.5 MHz, then 56/46, then 60/50. Class A is 79/66, then 73/60. The LISN is 50 µH / 50 Ω. Measure each line to ground. The lower limit applies at the edge.

cards.title: You can be told to stop
cards.body: There is no vested right to a frequency. Do not cause harmful interference, and accept interference from licensed stations, other Part 15 devices, ISM, and incidental radiators. Stop when the Commission says the device is causing harmful interference. The limits do not guarantee that interference is impossible.

cards.title: Authorization and the label
cards.body: Most unintentional radiators are SDoC or Certification. Scanning receivers, radar detectors, and Access BPL need Certification. The usual label has two conditions: do not cause harmful interference, and accept any interference. The manual warns that unapproved changes can void authority to operate.

cards.title: Exemptions are narrow
cards.body: Section 15.103 lists vehicles, certain utility and industrial controls, appliances, test equipment, specialized medical devices, 6 nW devices, and a few more. They stay under §15.5 and §15.29. A mix is exempt only when every device and every function is exempt. Retail medical gadgets are not exempt.

cards.title: How far to measure
cards.body: Unintentional radiators use ANSI C63.4-2014, with the clauses §15.31(a)(4) excludes. The upper frequency follows §15.33(b)(1). Unknown leads are 1 m long. Emissions more than 20 dB under the limit need not be reported unless another rule asks.

cards.title: Special accessories and home builds
cards.body: A shielded cable the product needs in order to comply has to ship with it, unless a professional installs it. Ordinary retail parts are not special, but the manual still has to name them. A home-built device skips authorization only if it is not sold, not a kit, and five or fewer for personal use. Section 15.5 still applies.
